titel: Mast Cells & Autism, Viral Skin Issues + Organs Aging Faster | Ask Me Anything

einzeiler: Cellular health, cold urticaria in children, and treatments for persistent hand warts.
kurzfassung: Dr. Will Cole and his team discuss cellular longevity and their new book, Heal Your Cells. They address a listener's question about a four-year-old child experiencing severe cold-induced hives alongside autism. They also evaluate holistic approaches for treating stubborn hand growths resembling warts.
stichpunkte: Introduction of the new book Heal Your Cells, focusing on cellular longevity and reversing accelerated biological aging.
Discussion of Stanford research showing one in five people have organs aging at uneven, rapid rates.
Exploration of the information model of aging, where cells lose recognition of self due to lifestyle and environmental factors.
Analysis of a listener's case regarding a four-year-old with autism experiencing cold urticaria and severe histamine reactions.
Recommendation of mast cell stabilizers like quercetin, stinging nettle, and dietary adjustments for managing histamine intolerance.
Discussion of a listener's persistent knuckle growths, exploring conventional and holistic treatments for suspected viral warts.
Emphasis on an inside-out approach to skin issues, targeting viral replication, nutrient deficiencies, and gut health.

clips.hook: One in five people have an organ aging significantly faster than others.
clips.text: Research from Stanford indicates that a substantial portion of the population experiences uneven organ aging, which significantly increases health risks.

clips.hook: People born after 1965 are aging faster than previous generations.
clips.text: Recent data from Nature Medicine reveals that younger generations exhibit accelerated biological aging compared to older cohorts at the same age.

clips.hook: Warts are typically caused by viral infections like HPV.
clips.text: Persistent skin bumps often stem from common viruses that take hold when the immune system struggles to mount an adequate defense.

clips.hook: Skin tags can be a sign of underlying insulin resistance.
clips.text: Dermatological manifestations often act as warning lights for internal metabolic imbalances taking place beneath the surface.

beschreibung:
In this Ask Me Anything episode, Dr. Will Cole and his team introduce Heal Your Cells (co-written with Dr. Josh Axe) and the Stanford research behind it, then answer two listener questions: what's driving cold urticaria and hives in a 4-year-old with autism, and what wart-like growths on the knuckles of a 23-year-old are really communicating about immune health. They cover mast cell activation, histamine protocols, salicylic acid, bee propolis, Manuka honey, and the gut-immune connection — plus a story about a beta fish named Huffle that becomes a surprisingly relevant mold PSA. For all links mentioned in this episode, visit http://www.drwillcole.com/podcast
